probe.format_note: 16:9 landscape (736x414, H.264, 24 fps), 63.3 s. Audio: AAC HE-AACv2 stereo 44.1 kHz at full level (volumedetect mean -17.4 dB, max 0.0 dB), so a real soundtrack (music bed assumed; content was not listened to and cut-to-beat alignment was not measured). The film ends on a held logo lockup from about 59.8 s to the end, with no fade to black inside the clip.

mode.why: third-party clip of unknown origin: borrow the motion language (one travelling light object carried through continuous camera moves, wipes by light and by foreground objects, scale matches) and the flat purple-night look only, never its illustrations, characters, story or logo (owner note). The clip is a narrated-style story film with characters (the history of an idea passed from person to person), which is EXPLAINER; a hook-problem-solution voiceover package may still run as REEL with the same grammar.

ignored.why: the story (a glowing idea passed through history from ancient builders, a philosopher, a scientist and a rocket launch to a modern recruiting office and a job-match app) and every drawn subject (hands, hills, stepped pyramid, caped figure, bearded thinker, lab, microscope, rocket, observatory, planets, auditorium, receptionist, gallery of framed pictures, trophies, profile UI) are the reference's content; never copied, setting and subjects come from the voice-over

the third-party brand mark «[id]entifiers», its bracket logo and the English UI labels («Jameson Block», «Key Skills», «Job search», «Compatibility») are another company's identity; never used. The film's own logo outro comes from the brand (router conflict order, item 5)

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2 over the whole clip (8 sheets of 4x4, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 10 frames at 13.75-14.0 (light-beam wipe), 40.08, 41.83, 49.21-49.25 (foreground-pillar wipe), 54.33 and 55.75; dense sheets at fps=5-8 on 1.5-4.5, 5.5-9.0, 9.0-12.0, 13.0-16.5, 17.5-20.5, 21.0-24.5, 25.0-28.0, 29.0-32.5, 34.5-37.5, 38.0-41.0, 44.0-47.0, 48.5-50.5 and 53.8-59.6 s, all viewed; audio level checked with volumedetect. Spans are accurate to about ±0.15 s. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: Flat vector story animation in a purple night world. Medium: 2D illustration (solid fills, a few thin line-art strokes, light grain), staged in layered planes and animated with continuous camera moves. Characters are simple flat figures (white skin, navy clothing, violet hair) with small cut-out style pose changes and blinks, never walking cycles in close shots. Typography: none apart from a brand mark at the end (ignored). Rhythm: 19 shots in 63.3 s (average about 3.3 s, range 1.4-4.7 s); only four hard cuts (40.08, 41.83, 54.33, 55.75 s), all in the second half; everything else joins by continuous camera moves (pull-backs, push-ins, trucks, tilts), scale matches, a diagonal light-beam wipe and foreground-object wipes. Moves are smooth: entrances ease-out, pushes and trucks ease-in-out about 0.4-0.9 s, follow moves linear, small wipes about 0.3-0.6 s; very little overshoot. Palette: deep navy and violet-indigo as the world, periwinkle for interiors, pale lime as the one glowing accent (the travelling light, light shafts, rim lines, stars), white for skin and bright surfaces, small orange accents. Signature moments: a single glowing light travels through the whole film (orb → sun disc → star → constellation → screen) and is passed from character to character; the light-beam wipe; points gathering into a line-art symbol; the final frame shrinking into the logo.
look: Flat 2D with 2.5D staging: solid fills, no cast shadows and no light direction on objects, depth shown by layered planes with parallax, darker navy silhouettes in front of lighter backgrounds, and atmospheric colour (sky gradients). The only soft effects are bloom glows on light sources (orb, star, beam, line icon, logo) and a fine grain or stipple texture on planets, bushes and the sky. Thin pale or lime rim lines outline silhouettes against dark areas. No depth-of-field blur, no 3D, no materials. Backgrounds are vertical colour gradients (violet sky, navy space, night to near-black) or flat periwinkle interiors.
code_translation: Code-native, flat. Build each scene as stacked SVG or canvas planes (sky gradient, far, mid, near, foreground) inside one camera group; camera moves are transforms on the planes with per-plane factors for parallax (pull-back = scale down, push = scale up toward a focus point, truck = translateX with near planes faster, tilt = translateY). The travelling light is one persistent element above all scenes (circle with radial gradient and a blur-filter bloom) that is handed from scene to scene. Wipes: a diagonal polygon mask with a feathered glowing edge for the light beam (about 0.3 s in, 0.3 s out); a large foreground silhouette or object that crosses the frame and acts as the mask edge for foreground wipes. Constellation: point sprites tween to path vertices, then SVG paths draw on with stroke-dashoffset plus a glow filter. Interface panels: semi-transparent rounded rects with staggered scale/fade entrances, bar width and fill colour tied to one value. Characters: flat cut-out parts with a few pose tweens (arm raise, point, wave), blink and mouth swaps; no full turnarounds. Grain: a subtle noise overlay or feTurbulence fill on planets and sky. Reference colours are mapped onto brand colour roles (world dark, world mid, interior light, glowing accent, warm accent), never used as literal hex values. No 3D, no shadows, no lens blur — the reference is flat, so the film stays flat.
continuity: One travelling light: a single glowing object persists across scenes and changes role (held object, sun disc behind a figure, a star, the dots of a symbol, a screen glow); the camera follows it, so the film reads as one journey.
Hand-off between characters: the light is tossed, caught or passed from one figure to the next, linking people across places and times without cuts.
Scene rises from the bottom edge: a new ground, its props and its character slide up into frame while the anchor object stays fixed.
Camera travels through depth: forward dollies pass foreground figures out of frame and reach the next subject in the same layered space.
Scale match: a tiny shape on the horizon (or a glow inside an icon) grows under a push-in or pull-back into the next scene's main object or screen.
Light-beam wipe: a bright diagonal wedge sweeps in, the new scene is revealed inside it and keeps it as its light; a dark wedge sweeps it away.
Lateral truck through one continuous set: two places share a ground band so a single sideways move joins them.
Tilt to travel: the subject stays centred while ground, sky and planets stream past at different speeds, then the subject leaves the frame and the camera settles on the next idea.
Gather into a symbol: one light multiplies into scattered points that connect into a line-art icon, which then gains orbit rings that echo the opening.
Foreground-object wipes: a near shoulder or a near pillar crosses the lens and acts as the cut.
Frame becomes the mark: the final scene shrinks inside the brand mark's shape at the end.
risks: Third-party film of unknown origin: ADAPT only. Never copy its subjects (orb in hands, stepped monument, philosopher, lab, rocket, planets, auditorium, receptionist, gallery, job-match UI), its history-of-an-idea story one to one, its characters, its logo or its UI labels; only the camera grammar, continuity devices, timing and the flat purple-night look.

Source is 16:9 (736x414); the film is usually 9:16. Vertical moves (rise from bottom, tilt up with streaming planets, stacked steps, constellation) translate directly; lateral trucks and wide multi-figure frames must be recomposed (tighter crops, trucks turned into tilts or pushes), keeping the parallax-plane idea.

The reference has almost no text: Persian on-screen text must be added in calm areas (sky, empty space, screen or panel surfaces), held long enough to read and kept inside the safe zone; text must not ride on fast parallax planes.

Character acting (turning, gesturing, hand-to-chin) is hand-animated in the source; in code keep characters to a few cut-out pose tweens, blinks and slides, and avoid turnarounds and walk cycles in close shots.

Glow is the signature light: brand colours replace the purple/lime pair (dark world role plus one bright accent role for the travelling light); banned brand colours are never used even where the reference has them (orange accents, lime glow are mapped to brand-safe roles).
The logo-outro technique (frame shrinks into the mark) touches brand identity: the brand's own logo outro wins; the technique is only offered if the brand has none.
The audio track is full-level and was not listened to; cut-to-beat alignment was not measured, so L6 builds sound from the storyboard and voice timing places every cut.
Colours and timings were read by eye from contact sheets (about ±0.15 s), not sampled or measured per frame.
